title: Modern art has been informed about gravity.
description: Sling Nouveau begins with a pleasingly unreasonable idea: what if a sculptural playground also invited you to knock things down?

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Sling Nouveau begins with a pleasingly unreasonable idea: what if a sculptural playground also invited you to knock things down?
The immediate priority is the slingshot. It should be easy to grab, satisfying to pull, and simple to position. Your thumb should be planning the shot, not negotiating access to the controls.
We’re also exploring tougher materials and specialized balls, so choosing how to hit something becomes part of the fun.
First comes the feeling of a great shot. Then we give you increasingly interesting reasons to take another.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: The rematch should not require technical support.
description: The website table has a deliberately simple brief: one fixed deal, as many attempts as you like.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The website table has a deliberately simple brief: one fixed deal, as many attempts as you like.
Same starting cards. Same challenge. Different decisions—and, ideally, an increasingly suspicious look at the move you made three turns ago.
The browser work is focused on reliable play, readable cards, and a restart that takes you cleanly back to the beginning. We’re keeping the demo distinct from the broader Palace app.
A rematch should begin with a button, not a troubleshooting expedition.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Five cards. Plenty of opinions.
description: Euchre already provides enough uncertainty through the cards. The interface does not need to contribute.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Euchre already provides enough uncertainty through the cards. The interface does not need to contribute.
Our current design direction is a clearer table, easier-to-read information, and indicators that explain the game without parking themselves on top of it.
Trump should be obvious. Your partner’s role should be obvious. A mysterious floating letter should not become an unofficial fifth player.
Online play and rankings belong in the development conversation, not in the list of promises we casually declare finished.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Friendship, with penalty points.
description: Hearts has a lovely ability to make an innocent-looking card feel like a personal statement.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Hearts has a lovely ability to make an innocent-looking card feel like a personal statement.
The design brief is to keep that drama at the table: readable hands, understandable turns, and enough visual clarity to follow what is happening without wrestling the screen.
The interface should help you enjoy the decisions, not make them for you.
We can aim for a friendlier experience. We cannot promise your friends will appreciate the queen of spades.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Confidence is not a bidding strategy. Apparently.
description: Spades deserves a table that respects the partnership.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Spades deserves a table that respects the partnership.
The bid, the score, the current trick, and your next action should be easy to understand. Everything else needs a good reason to occupy the screen.
Our design target is the rhythm of a satisfying card game: read the situation, make the decision, watch it unfold, and quietly reconsider how confident you sounded earlier.
The cards should provide the suspense. Finding the right button should not.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: One more deal. Entirely your own idea.
description: Solitaire should feel pleasantly inevitable: see the move, move the card, enjoy the little moment when everything starts to line up.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Solitaire should feel pleasantly inevitable: see the move, move the card, enjoy the little moment when everything starts to line up.
The current direction is cleaner presentation, more comfortable card sizes, and smoother movement. The board should feel calm without looking asleep.
We’re giving the classic its own polished place in the 4OH family.
No motivational speech required. Sometimes the reward is simply a tidy column and the deeply unreasonable conviction that you have time for another game.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Let the cards cause the trouble.
description: War does not need a complicated introduction. It needs a dependable entrance, a clear table, and a satisfying flip.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: War does not need a complicated introduction. It needs a dependable entrance, a clear table, and a satisfying flip.
The development priority is getting that basic rhythm right: stable play, readable cards, and battles that feel lively rather than sluggish.
The competition should come from what turns over—not from whether the interface cooperates.
Broader online ambitions remain development work unless verified. For now, the brief is wonderfully direct: make the familiar game feel good.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: A dragon is not a chore-management app.
description: A dragon should make you want to take off.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: A dragon should make you want to take off.
The current direction puts the emphasis on easier flight, clearer combat controls, a world worth moving through, and fire that deserves the name.
We’re pushing away from crowded controls and routine busywork toward the pleasure of going somewhere spectacular and doing something distinctly dragon-shaped when you arrive.
Progression should support that experience, not bury it under errands.
Online dragon-versus-dragon combat remains an ambition to develop—not a feature to announce before it works.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Your thumb has declined additional paperwork.
description: Thumb Command has a very clear staffing arrangement: one thumb, quite a lot of responsibility.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Thumb Command has a very clear staffing arrangement: one thumb, quite a lot of responsibility.

The interface needs to respect that. We’re aiming for a brighter, cleaner presentation, stronger ship selection, more distinctive enemies and bases, and less clutter between the player and the action.
The exciting decisions should happen in the defense of the world, not in an overcrowded strip of controls.
A busy spaceship is good. A busy interface needs to make its case.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: A dinosaur needs room to make an entrance.
description: Bobby’s world should feel lively before the first enemy arrives.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Bobby’s world should feel lively before the first enemy arrives.
The current direction includes a more expressive home screen, stronger battlefield artwork, easier zooming, and more interesting approaches for incoming enemies.
We also want the scene to stay composed when players move around it. Objects wandering away from the visible play area are not an advanced enemy strategy.
The goal is cheerful spectacle with a readable battlefield: enough personality to make you smile, enough clarity to help you defend it.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: We would like the towers to be a little less normal.
description: The blade tower has set an inconveniently entertaining standard.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The blade tower has set an inconveniently entertaining standard.
That is the creative direction we want more of: towers with distinct behavior and personality, not a row of interchangeable objects politely firing at things.
The workbench priorities include richer battlefield detail, useful close-up zoom, more expressive placement areas, and a cleaner way to choose and understand upgrades.
We want players thinking, “What does that one do?”
Preferably followed by, “Oh, that is ridiculous. I need it.”

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: A city, not a directory of buttons.
description: BooYang City should invite you to look around and choose somewhere to go.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: BooYang City should invite you to look around and choose somewhere to go.
The direction is a connected, full-screen place with destinations that feel like part of a neighborhood: the bakery, boutique, school, zoo, and the next interesting door.
We’re aiming for better visual scale, clearer interactions, and more personality in the places themselves.
The enjoyable question is “Where shall we go?”
It should not be “Which of these nearly identical rectangles contains the city?”

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: The planning department has rejected beige.
description: Funky Town needs room to be itself.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Funky Town needs room to be itself.
The current design push is toward a less cramped play space, more expressive buildings, and a town that feels like somewhere you are making—not a control panel you are filling out.
The visual ambition is playful and distinctive. The interaction still needs to be clear.
We want the neighborhood to develop a personality as you work on it.
Respectable urban planning is welcome. Excessive normality may require a permit.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Shorter name. Unreasonably enthusiastic explosions.
description: The name going forward is Unicorn Blast.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The name going forward is Unicorn Blast.
The development direction is brighter, smoother, and easier to understand: stronger home and campaign screens, satisfying effects, and tools that explain what they do before you have to guess.
Bombs and boosters should be fun because you understand the opportunity—not because you accidentally discover what that sparkling object was for.
We’re chasing the moment when a good move becomes a glorious chain reaction.
The unicorns deserve a rescue with a little production value.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: The shoes have been asked to remain on the feet.
description: A beautiful dress-up game depends on details that cannot be negotiated away: fit, scale, layering, and characters who feel alive.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: A beautiful dress-up game depends on details that cannot be negotiated away: fit, scale, layering, and characters who feel alive.
The current priorities include better-aligned outfits, a stronger wardrobe, more expressive princess presentation, and a home screen where the surrounding world actually surrounds her.
The bakery and decorating experiences need the same care. A cake should look worth decorating. A ballroom should feel worth filling.
The ambition is an inviting creative world—not a collection of pretty pieces that cannot quite agree where to stand.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: We have not established a maximum number of flowers.
description: Unicorn Land Adventures has its own creative brief: unicorns to personalize, habitats to shape, details to discover, and room to make something wonderfully yours.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Unicorn Land Adventures has its own creative brief: unicorns to personalize, habitats to shape, details to discover, and room to make something wonderfully yours.
It is a separate game from Unicorn Blast, with a different pace and a different kind of play.
The design challenge is making creation feel inviting rather than complicated. Choosing a look or decorating a space should lead naturally to another enjoyable idea.
The flower limit remains an artistic question, not an engineering recommendation.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Less spreadsheet. More bedside manner.
description: The Amigo is the point.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The Amigo is the point.
We’re shaping a sleep companion that can react to the information actually available, offer a useful observation, and sound like someone you would willingly hear from in the morning.
That means clearer presentation, a more expressive pillow character, and commentary that can be warm and cheeky without making things up.
Available sleep-stage information should not be ignored just because a long-term pattern is still developing. Missing data should be acknowledged, not invented.
The aim is better understanding—not a diagnosis delivered by a pillow.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Your next counteroffer deserves better than “Um.”
description: SOVINTO is built around an understandable ambition: help people prepare for conversations that matter.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: SOVINTO is built around an understandable ambition: help people prepare for conversations that matter.
The current foundation includes local preparation and general prewritten help. Richer practice and live AI guidance remain development work unless a newer build verifies otherwise.
We want the experience to make priorities clearer and the next step less intimidating.
Not every negotiation needs a dramatic boardroom. Sometimes it begins with a difficult question and a moment to collect your thoughts.
That moment deserves a useful tool.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Twenty open tabs is not a research strategy.
description: Whomly’s direction is to turn scattered public professional information into useful context.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Whomly’s direction is to turn scattered public professional information into useful context.
Who is relevant? What supports that conclusion? What would make a thoughtful next conversation?
We’re interested in a clearer path from discovery to understanding—not an impressive-looking pile of unexplained results.
The product should help people organize evidence and prepare, while respecting the difference between public professional research and someone’s private life.
A useful briefing should leave you better informed, not merely in possession of several more tabs.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: A table with room to think.
description: Gin Rummy is a two-player game. The interface should leave room for the decisions.

body.heading: On the workbench
paragraphs: Gin Rummy is a two-player game. The interface should leave room for the decisions: read the hand, spot the sets and runs, draw, and choose what to let go.

The website now shows a real development-build preview alongside the separately labeled concept artwork. Development testing covers joining a table, drawing, discarding, and recovering a match after a restart. That is evidence from development testing, not a public online launch.
Our brief is a clear table and reliable recovery, with the cards doing the interesting work. Public hosting and downloadable builds still need their own checks before we offer them.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Before the dragons, there were cards.
description: Before there were dragons to steer, cities to build, or unicorns requiring an unreasonable amount of creative attention, there were cards.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Before there were dragons to steer, cities to build, or unicorns requiring an unreasonable amount of creative attention, there were cards.

Palace, Hearts, Spades, and Euchre gave Four of Hearts its starting table. Familiar games. Different personalities. Plenty of opportunities to discover that “just make the cards work” is not, technically speaking, a development plan.

The important questions were wonderfully ordinary. Can you read your hand? Do you know whose turn it is? Does the game explain itself without delivering a lecture? Can you get to the enjoyable part before your tea becomes a historical artifact?
Those questions still follow us into every new project.
Four of Hearts became 4OH when the name was said out loud. No encrypted founder prophecy. No seventeen-slide branding revelation. Just a name that sounded right.
The ambitions have grown considerably. The basic test has not: does this feel good to use, and is it worth coming back for?
Pull up a chair. This is where the workbench story begins.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: The card table got a little out of hand.
description: A sensible studio might add another card game and call it a productive afternoon.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: A sensible studio might add another card game and call it a productive afternoon.
Our workbench now includes dragons, defensive towers, a heroic dinosaur, princess wardrobes, entire towns, and several unicorn-related responsibilities.
The card table did not disappear. It acquired some very unusual neighbors.

The expanding lineup has brought different design problems with it. A card game needs clarity and rhythm. A flying dragon needs convincing movement. A creative world needs room to explore. A princess wardrobe needs the shoes to maintain a professional relationship with the feet.
These are not interchangeable problems, and the games should not feel like the same template wearing different hats.
What connects them is the aim: make the interaction inviting, the personality memorable, and the next thing you want to do obvious.
We are building a family of games, not a warehouse of icons.
Somewhere along the way, the workbench became a neighborhood. Apparently we are responsible for the zoning now.

author: The 4OH Workshop
historicalPeriod: From the card table to original worlds

title: A U has entered the chat.
description: A brief developer detour into Canadian English, where “colour” brings an extra letter and “centre” rearranges the furniture.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: A brief developer detour into Canadian English, where “colour” brings an extra letter and “centre” rearranges the furniture.
We like this. Even the spelling gets a little customization.

Canadian English often keeps the U in words such as “colour” and “favour,” while favoring endings such as “centre” and “theatre.” That does not make it a separate language, and it certainly does not mean every Canadian writes exactly the same way.
It does give a software studio something entertaining to think about between moving buttons three pixels to the left.
There is a real design point hiding under the extra vowel: words should feel natural to the people reading them. A label is not finished merely because it fits in a rectangle.
Our preferred international policy is straightforward: make people welcome, make the instructions clear, and never charge extra for the U.
That would be a microtransactioun.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Fewer buttons. More “one more go.”
description: The workbench has a recurring request: give the enjoyable part more room.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The workbench has a recurring request: give the enjoyable part more room.

More room for the dragon to fly. More room for the city to feel like a city. More room to see the cards. More room to pull back a slingshot without conducting a delicate archaeological excavation with your thumb.
This is not a campaign against useful features. It is a campaign against making every useful feature stand in the doorway at once.
Across the projects, the direction is clearer controls, calmer screens, more expressive artwork, and interactions that make sense before an instruction panel starts clearing its throat.
The same principle applies to our apps. Sleep information should feel understandable. Research should become useful context. Preparation should make a difficult conversation less difficult.
A screen does not earn its keep by containing more things.
It earns its keep when you know what to do next—and actually want to do it.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: BooYang City: a town that grows with play
description: Animal friends, pastry inventions, go-karts, and new places to explore are taking shape in the development build.
imageAlt: BooYang City development artwork

body.heading: September 11–12: from feeding fixes to new adventures
paragraphs: Published September 12, 2026. A September 11 checkpoint repaired animal feeding. The September 12 development build extends that everyday play into a growing toy town.

body.heading: A small beginning, a bigger world
paragraphs: The animal center can grow into a zoo and nature reserve, opening go-kart trails and helicopter exploration. The bakery grows through pastry inventions into a restaurant and a five-star rooftop tasting party. Familiar care, recipes, and placement activities remain available.

body.heading: What we have checked
paragraphs: The full growth paths and saved progress were exercised in the browser. On a Samsung phone, the latest build passed feeding and play, the first expansion, recipe saving, and return after a cold launch. Higher-stage kart, helicopter, and restaurant play still needs further device testing. This is development progress, not a public app release.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: GildenSpire: a dragon built to move
description: An original animated dragon, richer terrain, and a completed native campaign check move the world forward.
imageAlt: GildenSpire dragon-flight concept artwork

body.heading: September 12: movement, models, and a world to fly through
paragraphs: Published September 12, 2026. The latest development checkpoint brings an original rigged dragon with 17 animation clips, leafy trees, a more detailed tower, and reworked islands and alpine terrain.

body.heading: Making movement belong to the creature
paragraphs: This pass repaired flight poses, animation transitions, species ornaments, and effects attached to the dragon. It also addressed floating terrain details and an obstruction in the practice area.

body.heading: Progress with work still ahead
paragraphs: The candidate build passed its fresh-player and campaign checks on a Samsung phone, including victories, defeat, retry, and saved-game reload. Art polish, more distinct species anatomy, and sustained performance testing remain unfinished. The images here show the established visual direction; they are not screenshots of every new asset. No public release date has been announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Small fixes that change the feel
description: Battle speed, sleep refreshes, saved progress, and creative tools received focused attention in the latest audit.
imageAlt: Four of Hearts Interactive studio mark

body.heading: September 12: careful engineering in practice
paragraphs: Published September 12, 2026. Recent work focused on how the apps behave when you actually use them: changing a setting, returning to a game, refreshing information, or saving something you made.

body.heading: A battle at your pace
paragraphs: Evil Doom Boy’s development build now offers 0.5×, 1×, 2×, and 4× battle speed. Changing speed while paused keeps the battle paused. The controls and combat behavior were checked in the browser and on a Samsung phone.

body.heading: A refresh that finishes
paragraphs: Sleep Amigo received fixes for refresh completion and an unnecessary write that could leave a finished refresh waiting. Repeated refreshes and a process restart passed on the tested Samsung. Broader device and provider testing remains to be done.

body.heading: The details deserve attention
paragraphs: The same audit addressed card-game timing and controls, Princess Land room-photo readiness, and Unicorn Land photo and landscape-entry issues. These were focused development checks—not certification that every app or feature is ready for release.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: AI in the workshop—and in useful products
description: How AI-assisted development and carefully chosen product capabilities fit our old-school values.
imageAlt: SOVINTO negotiation app emblem

body.heading: September 12: a note from the workbench
paragraphs: Published September 12, 2026. We use AI to help explore ideas, write and review software, and test our work. It expands what an independent studio can attempt; human judgment still sets the direction.

body.heading: Two different roles
paragraphs: AI-assisted development does not mean every product contains an AI engine. Whomly includes an optional AI-assisted public research and briefing workflow. SOVINTO’s live negotiation guidance engine is being developed, with preparation and general prewritten help as its current foundation.

body.heading: Useful before impressive
paragraphs: SOVINTO’s aim is practical: prepare for conversations such as a new job offer or buying a house, then find useful guidance when you need it. Its live AI guidance and interactive practice remain under development. We consider privacy and data flow alongside usefulness, and describe capabilities product by product.

body.heading: Still on the workbench
paragraphs: Funky Town’s next city-building and creativity-pressure redesign is also in progress. We will share completed milestones as they are verified. Old-school values, modern ambitions, and careful engineering remain the thread through the work.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Introducing GildenSpire: Flight or Fight
description: Raise a dragon, take direct control in the sky, and discover what happens when flying becomes fighting.
imageAlt: A red GildenSpire dragon and rider flying toward a vast fantasy world as a rival approaches

body.heading: Considerably bigger wings
paragraphs: Four of Hearts Interactive is building something with considerably bigger wings.
GildenSpire begins with a simple idea: raise a dragon, climb onto its back, and discover what happens when the world stops being something you walk through and becomes something you fly over.

body.heading: Flying is gameplay
paragraphs: Raising your dragon matters. Training matters. Discovering new dragons matters. But the heart of GildenSpire is what happens once you take off.

You will climb, dive, bank through mountain passes, cross enormous landscapes, discover places hidden from the ground, and eventually encounter other creatures that are not particularly interested in sharing the sky.
Then flying becomes fighting.
That is GildenSpire.
Flight or fight.
And we are only beginning to build the world.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Why Flying Has to Be Fun
description: The journey should be gameplay: direct flight, enormous terrain, curiosity, and combat that rewards control.
imageAlt: A rider directly controlling a red dragon over islands, castles, mountains, and waterfalls

body.heading: Getting somewhere should be part of the fun
paragraphs: There is a simple rule behind GildenSpire: getting somewhere should be part of the fun.
We do not want players to press a destination button and watch a dragon animation while the next screen loads.
We want you flying the dragon.

body.heading: Stay in the sky
paragraphs: We want mountains to feel enormous when you skim past them. We want diving toward an island to feel fast. We want you banking around towers, threading through ruins, climbing through clouds, and spotting something in the distance that makes you change direction just to see what it is.
And when combat begins, those same flying skills should matter.
A great dragon game should make you want to stay in the sky even when there is nowhere you are required to go.
That is one of the standards we are building GildenSpire around.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Building Dragons That Actually Feel Different
description: GildenSpire dragons are being designed as different creatures—not one model wearing different colors.
imageAlt: A collection of substantially different dragon species planned for GildenSpire

body.heading: Another dragon, not another skin
paragraphs: One red dragon, one blue dragon, one green dragon.
That is not enough.
GildenSpire is being designed around dragons that should actually feel different.
Different bodies. Different wings. Different movement. Different strengths. Different abilities. Different personalities.

body.heading: Different ways to fly and fight
paragraphs: A powerful fire dragon might feel heavy and aggressive in the air. A smaller air dragon might turn faster and climb differently. An ice dragon might completely change how a team approaches a fight.
The goal is not simply to collect another skin.
The goal is to discover another dragon.
And somewhere beyond all of them is the Golden Egg.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: From Search to Opportunity: Building Whomly
description: How a search-first interface can turn public professional research into useful context and a thoughtful next step.
imageAlt: Whomly interface showing public professional search, profiles, AI-assisted context, and outreach preparation

body.heading: Start with the question
paragraphs: Whomly begins with the person you are trying to find: a general counsel in Chicago, a healthcare innovation leader, a potential board member, or a specialist whose public work fits the problem in front of you.
The search interface is being designed to accept useful professional criteria without turning research into an endless directory.

body.heading: Public research, organized
paragraphs: The hard part is rarely finding one more public page. It is understanding why a person may be relevant. Whomly is designed to organize publicly available professional information into readable context, saved people, and lists the user controls.

AI-assisted summaries and outreach drafts may help with the work, but the boundary matters: public professional context in, user-reviewed preparation out. No private-profile access, automatic contact, or release date is being claimed.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Welcome to BooYang City
description: A connected city gives us room for a zoo, bakery, boutique, school, hospital, and almost anything fun that might open next.
imageAlt: BooYang City artwork featuring a cheerful character and a colorful city of destinations

body.heading: A city is better than a menu
paragraphs: BooYang City is our framework for putting many different kinds of play inside one connected place. You look across the map, choose somewhere interesting, and enter a destination that has its own activity, characters, and progression.
The first destination ideas include the Zoo, Bakery, Boutique, School, and Hospital. Each should feel different, but every visit should make the larger city feel more alive.

body.heading: Begin with a tiny bakery
paragraphs: The Bakery captures the wider loop. Start small, learn recipes, serve customers, improve the kitchen, decorate the room, and gradually grow toward a café or restaurant. The place should visibly change because the player spent time there.
Opening a new destination should feel like opening a new toy box. BooYang City is in development, with no public build, platform, or release date announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Introducing Thumb Command: Save Planet Earth
description: Meet Blueguard and the worldwide arcade-defense campaign taking shape at Four of Hearts Interactive.
imageAlt: Blueguard interceptor defending Chicago from a purple alien invasion

body.heading: The city is the base
paragraphs: Thumb Command is a fast, colourful arcade-defense game in development around one clear mission: save Planet Earth.
Chicago, San Francisco, New York, London, and Tokyo establish the current campaign direction. No public build, store listing, or release date has been announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Making Sleep Data Feel Human
description: Sleep Readiness, Tonight’s Game Plan, Ask Amigo, Wind Down, and a small celestial companion give the numbers some warmth.
imageAlt: Sleep Amigo celestial companion and dark premium sleep guidance interface

body.heading: A score needs an explanation
paragraphs: A sleep score can be tidy and still leave a person wondering what to do next. Sleep Amigo is being built around that next question.
Sleep Readiness offers a quick assessment. Tonight’s Game Plan turns available information into a few things worth considering. Ask Amigo makes the experience a conversation instead of a spreadsheet.

body.heading: Sophisticated software can still have warmth
paragraphs: The new visual direction brings together midnight blues, aurora colour, clear glassy panels, and a small celestial Amigo who feels calm rather than clinical. Wind Down and Trends complete the current product idea.
Sleep Amigo remains in development. It is wellness software, not a medical device, and supported wearables or health sources will be named only after implementation is verified.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Building a Town That Refuses to Look Normal
description: Funky Town treats buildings as canvases and progression as a chance to make every neighborhood more expressive.
imageAlt: Funky Town artwork showing a bold neighborhood transformed by murals, color, music, and street art

body.heading: Buildings can become canvases
paragraphs: Many city builders begin with different intentions and slowly converge on the same neat grid. Funky Town begins with the opposite question: what if progress made the place stranger, louder, and more personal?
Murals, graffiti, sculpture, music, unusual architecture, parks, studios, cafés, rooftop gardens, and gathering places can give each district a different identity.

body.heading: Progress should change the view
paragraphs: The goal is not simply to make every building larger. It is to let players transform neighborhoods through creative decisions until two long-running Funky Towns could look dramatically different.
Community matters as much as colour. People and the places where they meet are what make the art feel alive. Funky Town is in development, with no public build or release date announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Building Unicorn Land Adventures
description: Unicorn creation, magical habitats, decorating, discovery, and mini-games define a distinct creative game.
imageAlt: Unicorn Land Adventures habitat

body.heading: Current development direction
paragraphs: Unicorn Land begins with character creation and grows into habitats, gardens, discoveries, and mini-games.
No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Inside Princess Land Adventures
description: Character style, castle rooms, cooking, decorating, and mini-games begin forming one creative game.
imageAlt: Princess Land Adventures castle world

body.heading: Current development direction
paragraphs: Princess Land explores character styling, castle building, room decoration, cooking, and approachable mini-games.
No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: People Lens Is Becoming Whomly
description: The working name is retiring. Whomly better fits the journey from discovery to context to possible opportunity.
imageAlt: Whomly product identity and public-information people discovery interface

body.heading: A name that fits the whole idea
paragraphs: People Lens was a useful working name for a search concept. As the product grew toward profiles, context, lists, and outreach preparation, the name stopped describing the complete job.
The permanent product identity is Whomly. The old public route will keep forwarding here, but current navigation, metadata, product pages, and artwork now use the new name.

body.heading: Discover. Understand. Connect.
paragraphs: Whomly is about finding relevant people in publicly available professional sources, understanding why they may matter to a search, and organizing a possible next step.
That also means respecting the line between public research and private information. We are building the useful side of the line.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: HeartStack Unicorn Blast Joins the Workbench
description: A first look at colourful combos, crystal cages, boosters, and unicorn rescue.
imageAlt: HeartStack Unicorn Blast colourful match board

body.heading: Current build direction
paragraphs: HeartStack combines colourful matching with cascading combos, boosters, crystal cages, and unicorn rescue sequences.
No public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Evil Doom Boy: Two Heroes, One Fight
description: Evil Doom Boy is one action-adventure game with Evil Doom Boy as the default hero and Evil Doom Girl as the alternate hero.
imageAlt: Evil Doom Boy and alternate playable hero Evil Doom Girl facing Evil Doom

body.heading: Choose who stands up to Evil Doom
paragraphs: Evil Doom is closing in. Begin as Evil Doom Boy or switch to Evil Doom Girl, then run, fight, swing, and survive long enough to stop it.
Evil Doom Boy is one game with two selectable heroes. The project remains in development; no public build, store availability, or release date has been announced.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Bobby and the Breadstone
description: Bread-powered towers, branching paths, cheerful enemies, and one heroic dinosaur define Bobby’s direction.
imageAlt: Bobby the Breadasaurus tower-defense gameplay

body.heading: A small hero holds a very busy path
paragraphs: Bobby the Breadasaurus is a tower-defense adventure about placing bread-powered towers and protecting the Breadstone.

author: The 4OH Workshop

title: Why We’re Building Sleep Amigo
description: The harder sleep problem is not collecting another number. It is understanding what may matter tonight.
imageAlt: Sleep Amigo concept board with its celestial guide and nightly sleep interfaces

body.heading: A nightly conversation, not another dashboard
paragraphs: Sleep apps can produce a remarkable amount of data. The harder problem is deciding what deserves attention before bed.
We are building Sleep Amigo to help turn available sleep information into a simple nightly conversation: what may have mattered, what seems to be changing, and what is worth considering tonight.

body.heading: Why an Amigo?
paragraphs: The idea needs more warmth than a chart. A small celestial companion gives the product a voice without making the interface childish. The goal is premium sleep technology with someone friendly waiting inside it.
Sleep Amigo remains an in-development wellness concept. It does not diagnose conditions, replace professional advice, or claim unverified device compatibility.
